title: On Grabbing the rope with both hands
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：grab　|　正文 354 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 grab 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1950 the gardener ① grabbed the rope with both hands with great care, and every apprentice in the garden said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three springs on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the gardener ② grabs the rope with both hands on the same day without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ grab the rope with both hands at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ grabbed the rope with both hands before — a line in the notebook for April 1944 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Grabbing the rope with both hands with great care, the gardener said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the trowel at the far bed, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ grab the best place by the fire on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Grab the best place by the fire at once and never mention it again.

By 1957 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the notebook, and a new apprentice from the next garden ⑧ grabs the best place by the fire with great care every spring without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the bed, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ grabbed the rope with both hands again when nobody else would.

⑩ To grab the rope with both hands, my mother said in 1962, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the garden remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the garden forgets, somebody grabs the rope with both hands on the same day again and somebody must grab the rope with both hands with great care all over again.

grab 意为“抓住”，自那以后园丁当天就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 grabs。
grab 意为“抓住”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯抓住双手抓住那根绳子”，此处为不定式 to grab the rope with both hands。
grab 意为“抓住”，园艺笔记里 四月 那行字说明早在 1957 年之前就有人抓住过，故用过去完成时 had grabbed。
grab 意为“抓住”，园丁说“抓住双手抓住那根绳子这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 grabbing the rope with both hands 作主语。
grab 意为“抢走”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去抢走抢了炉边最好的位置”，should ever 之后用原形 grab the best place by the fire。
grab 意为“抢走”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻抢走抢了炉边最好的位置（grab the best place by the fire at once），以后再也不要提起。
grab 意为“抓住”，新来的学徒每个春天都照例抢走抢了炉边最好的位置，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 grabs。
grab 意为“抓住”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次小心翼翼地抓住双手抓住那根绳子，用一般过去式 grabbed 叙述。
grab 意为“抓住”，结尾那句是母亲 1962 年的话：要抓住双手抓住那根绳子，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和园子记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 grab 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1950 the gardener grabbed the rope with both hands with great care, and nobody in the garden forgot it.
Even now the gardener grabs the rope with both hands on the same day whenever the garden asks.
Grabbing the rope with both hands with great care, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever grab the best place by the fire on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new apprentice from the next garden grabs the best place by the fire with great care every spring, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother grabbed the rope with both hands again, and the garden remembered that half.
